uncited: It differs from standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by operating on surfels projected into screen space, accumulating color and geometric attributes via front-to-back alpha compositing [Parent].
- `colors`: Per-surfel colors, shape $[N, D]$ (where $D$ is color channels, typically 3) or spherical harmonic coefficients if `sh_degree` is provided.
- `isect_offsets`: Encoded intersection offsets for tile-based processing, shape $[C, \text{tile\_height}, \text{tile\_width}]$.
**Projection:** Project 2D Gaussian surfels to 2D screen space using `fully_fused_projection_2dgs`.
- Broadcast color coefficients to $[C, N, K, 3]$ (where $K$ is SH coefficient count).
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot H \cdot W)$ in the naive reference implementation, where $N$ is the number of surfels and $H, W$ are image dimensions.
Tile-based optimization reduces this to $O(K \cdot H \cdot W)$ where $K$ is the average number of surfels per tile.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N + H \cdot W)$ for storing surfel properties and output buffers.
- **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
- **Strengths:** Provides a clear, differentiable (via MLX autodiff in the reference) reference implementation for 2D Gaussian Splatting.
- **When to use:** For debugging, testing, and educational purposes.
For production, use the CUDA implementation.
- **When not to use:** When real-time performance is required and the CUDA implementation is not available.
The method is part of the 2D Gaussian Splatting framework, which extends 3D Gaussian Splatting by using surfels (2D Gaussians) instead of 3D ellipsoids.
